name: Kilo 43
story: Reverend Andreas’ congregation has met in his home since 2019. Although the C&MA National President viewed this location as a strategic spot for a church plant, they were initially discouraged to find that transporting building materials would be nearly impossible due to the lack of a stable road and bridge. CCC was able to help fund the ground leveling for the church plant and the construction of a new road leading to it.

name: Mustard Seed Saitama
story: International Workers Kevin and Nozomi West planted Mustard Seed Kobe in Nozomi’s home country of Japan in 2016. After sensing the Lord’s call to plant another church in Japan, the Wests left Kobe and are in the initial stages of planting Mustard Seed Saitama in Tokyo. CCC was able to help fund the startup of Mustard Seed Saitama, which will secure building space and Japanese church staff.

name: Samboja
story: Reverend Hendrik leads a small church community, and he and his wife host a tutoring after-school program for Muslim children. CCC helped purchase land for a church plant near the regional hospital and in the direction of the new harbor. The funds have already helped raise the profile of the church and the after-school program in the community.

name: Mustard Seed Sapporo
story: The Japanese are considered the second largest unreached people group in the world. Tanner and Delaney Salva began language school in Japan in 2020 and served at Mustard Seed Tokyo until 2024, when they felt God was calling them to plant Mustard Seed Church in Sapporo, Japan. CCC was able to help fund the startup of MS Sapporo, which will help secure building space and Japanese church staff.

name: Paser
story: This congregation serves the indigenous people of the new capital region. Reverend Demos leads the church. Because many land and business owners are Muslims, it can be challenging to hold Christian church services in these facilities. CCC provided funds for sand, stone, and a water tank for a new church building that opened for Christmas services in 2024.

name: Dionina
story: International Workers were pulled out of the country in 2022 because of terrorism and instability. However, the National Church is thriving, and God is at work! Pastor Daniel leads a congregation in a village where Jihadists are present. CCC was able to purchase a steel roof and pillars, while the congregation will finish the church building with mud bricks.

name: Dushanbe
story: This is a country in Central Asia where 99.5% of the people are considered unreached. Currently, there are thirty-eight house churches in its capital city, made up of Afghan refugees who have heard the Good News, responded, and are making disciples! CCC provided funds for a centralized church location for these church plants, which will offer a safe space for discipleship, leadership training, worship, and more!

name: Koch Lii
story: HOPE ALIVE! is a faith-based organization opening its fifth site in northern Uganda. The organization focuses on education for children and on farming and business for caretakers, but it knows that true transformation does not happen without partnership from a gospel-believing church. The funds from CCC will help fund community outreach, worship equipment, Bibles, Bible training for church workers, children’s curriculum, and more!

name: Nusantara
story: The fastest-growing Alliance church plant in Green City is also the newest! Pastor Helno and his family established a church plant near the new capital. Due to rapid growth, they outgrew their meeting place, a local café. With the help of funding from CCC, they will soon close on a piece of land, where they will build a new multi-purpose facility that will serve the community and provide meeting space for the church.

name: Beit Jala
story: The Beit Jala Alliance Church is part of the Evangelical Alliance Church of the Holy Lands. Reverends Jack Sara and Bassem Adranly lead a congregation of around fifty young adults. The church continues to grow steadily and is outgrowing its current rented facility. With the help of funding from CCC, they are purchasing land in order to build a church building.

name: New Life
story: Pastor Jeewan Moktan leads New Life Church, with a congregation of just over fifty people. In Nepal, care for the elderly is typically done within families, so those without families often end up homeless. With the help of funding from CCC, New Life will construct a building next to the church that will serve multiple purposes, including providing housing for up to twelve elderly individuals and serving as a biblical training and prayer center.

name: New Life
story: Pastor Akshya Rai leads New Life Church, a small congregation located in West Bengal, India. This new church plant is very focused on outreach, especially to the tribal people of Bhutan. With the help of funding from CCC, New Life will be able to build a one-room church building. Additionally, New Life in Omaha plans to partner with this church by helping support some of its ministries.

name: Kakata
story: Pastor Richard leads a small congregation of about twenty people in western Liberia. His church is situated in an area with three prominent unreached people groups: Gola, Maninka, and Vai. They are currently meeting in a stick building. With the help of funds from CCC, the church will not only be able to construct a building for its congregation to meet in, but also dig a well and a latrine and train evangelistic teams.

name: Serrekunda
story: Bivocational pastor Francis Moseray has planted three churches in The Gambia. The newest one is in Serrekunda, a very urban area of the country. Currently, 85 members attend the church plant. With funds from CCC, they will be able to construct a block church building and train and equip believers to go out into areas with little access to the gospel.
